name: TTrials
question: In older men with low testosterone and symptoms, does one year of testosterone gel improve sexual activity, walking ability, and vitality versus placebo?

design.population: Men aged 65 years or older with mean serum testosterone below 275 ng/dL and symptoms qualifying them for at least one of three main trials.
design.description: Multicenter, double-blind randomized placebo-controlled trial program
design.locator: Primary report, Methods: Study Design, Participants, Study Treatment; Results: Participants; AUA guideline, PSA Response to Testosterone Therapy, for allocation

verdictNote: Sexual activity improved; walking and vitality primary outcomes were not significant in their qualifying cohorts.
takeaway: In symptomatic older men with low testosterone, one year of titrated testosterone gel versus placebo improved sexual activity, desire, and erectile function; the prespecified walking and vitality primary outcomes did not improve significantly in their respective trials.

reports.label: Main trials report
reports.citation: Snyder PJ, Bhasin S, Cunningham GR, et al. "Effects of Testosterone Treatment in Older Men." *N Engl J Med.* 2016;374(7):611-624. doi:10.1056/NEJMoa1506119
reports.followUp: 12 months of treatment; adverse events collected through 12 additional months
reports.followUpLocator: Full text, Methods: Study Design and Oversight

results.measure: Month-12 mean change in PDQ-Q4 score; adjusted mean difference in change averaged across months 3–12
results.note: Sexual Function Trial cohort; the modeled effect averages all postbaseline visits, not just month 12.

results.endpoint: Six-minute walk improvement of at least 50 m
results.measure: Month-12 proportion; adjusted odds ratio averaged across months 3–12
results.note: Physical Function Trial cohort; odds ratio is the longitudinal model effect.

results.endpoint: FACIT-Fatigue improvement of at least 4 points
results.measure: Month-12 proportion; adjusted odds ratio averaged across months 3–12
results.note: Vitality Trial cohort; odds ratio is the longitudinal model effect.

results.measure: Month-12 mean change; adjusted mean difference in change averaged across months 3–12
Month-12 mean change; adjusted mean difference in change averaged across months 3–12

results.endpoint: Six-minute walk improvement of at least 50 m in all participants
results.measure: Month-12 proportion; adjusted odds ratio averaged across months 3–12
results.note: All-trials analysis, distinct from the Physical Function Trial primary analysis.

harms.label: PSA rise of at least 1.0 ng/mL during treatment
harms.note: Safety population; referral followed confirmed PSA rise or a prostate nodule.

harms.label: Hemoglobin at least 17.5 g/dL during treatment
Adjudicated major cardiovascular event during treatment
harms.note: Myocardial infarction, stroke, or cardiovascular death; the trial was too small for reliable risk estimation.

harms.label: IPSS above 19 during treatment
harms.note: Safety population; men with baseline IPSS above 19 were excluded.

delivery.label: Gel dosing and monitoring
delivery.value: AndroGel 1% started at 5 g daily; dose adjusted after central testosterone assays at months 1, 2, 3, 6, and 9 to target the young-adult normal range.

delivery.label: Treatment completion
delivery.locator: Full text, Results: Participants and Study Treatment

delivery.label: Prostate monitoring
delivery.value: PSA and digital rectal examination at months 3 and 12; PSA again at month 18; confirmed PSA rise of at least 1.0 ng/mL or nodule prompted urology referral.

reports.label: Sexual-function analysis
reports.citation: Cunningham GR, Stephens-Shields AJ, Rosen RC, et al. "Testosterone Treatment and Sexual Function in Older Men With Low Testosterone Levels." *J Clin Endocrinol Metab.* 2016;101(8):3096-3104. doi:10.1210/jc.2016-1645
reports.followUp: 12 months of treatment; sexual-function questionnaires every 3 months
reports.followUpLocator: Full text, Subjects and Methods: Study design, p 3097

results.endpoint: Measures of sexual activity improved versus placebo
results.measure: PDQ-Q4 component measures with significant treatment effects across months 3–12 in the 470-man Sexual Function Trial (234 testosterone, 236 placebo)

values.exp: 10 of 12 measures favored testosterone (P values <0.001 to 0.026)

results.note: Intention-to-treat analysis by assigned arm. The two nonsignificant components were flirting by others and daytime spontaneous erections; the paper does not tabulate component-level arm values or estimates.
results.locator: Full text, Results: Effect of the intervention on measures of sexual activity, pp 3099–3100; Figure 2A

results.endpoint: Sexual activity association with free testosterone change
results.measure: Adjusted PDQ-Q4 change per 20 pg/mL free testosterone increment within the testosterone arm
results.note: Within-arm hormone association, not a randomized treatment effect; total testosterone and estradiol increments were also associated with PDQ-Q4 change.

results.endpoint: Sexual desire association with free testosterone change
results.measure: Adjusted DISF-SDD change per 20 pg/mL free testosterone increment within the testosterone arm
results.note: Total testosterone and estradiol increments were also associated with desire; none of the three hormone increments was associated with IIEF-EFD change (P=0.98, 0.66, and 0.27, respectively).

results.endpoint: Orgasmic function association with estradiol change
results.measure: Adjusted IIEF-OFD change per 5 pg/mL estradiol increment within the testosterone arm
results.note: Total and free testosterone increments did not show significant associations with IIEF-OFD change.

results.endpoint: Predictors and hormone threshold for sexual-function response
results.measure: Interactions with 27 baseline characteristics after false-discovery-rate adjustment and within-arm threshold analyses
results.note: No baseline characteristic remained a significant response predictor after multiplicity adjustment; no sex-steroid response threshold was detected.
results.locator: Full text, Results: Participant characteristics affecting response and Relation of changes in hormone levels, pp 3100–3101

delivery.label: Sexual-function analysis gel dose target and adherence assessment
delivery.value: AndroGel 1% started at 5 g daily; testosterone target changed from 400–800 to 500–800 ng/dL; used and unused pump bottles were weighed to assess adherence.
delivery.locator: Full text, Subjects and Methods: Intervention, p 3097
